The fifth cluster gathers the person of Christ and the last things — the doctrines of continuation and completion: a life that does not end (§E.5.1), God entered into the world (§E.5.2), the dead raised (§E.5.3), and history closed in judgment (§E.5.4).

The shared measure is the book's account of what a person is: a finite, self-producing recursion whose death is its closure (§8.7.5), within a Nature that has no outside to arrive from and no channel to return through (§6.7.2–§6.7.3, Chapter 7). Each entry asks whether the promised continuation survives that account, and names what falls where it does not.
